description: Wavetable VCO: the Surge XT wavetable oscillator, morphing through a table of single-cycle waves with skew, saturation and formant shift

params.text: Sets the pitch in volts, added to the voltage at V/OCT; 0V gives middle C at 261.63Hz.
Sweeps through the frames of the wavetable, the first frame at the far left and the last at the far right.
Skews the waveform vertically, either way round.
Compresses the waveform in time while the cycle length stays put, shifting the formants by up to 60 semitones.
Skews the waveform horizontally, either way round.
Spreads the unison copies in pitch, over 100 cents, or 1200 cents when extended.
Sets how many detuned copies of the oscillator are stacked, 1 to 16; at 1 there is no unison.
Modulation depth into pitch, in octaves per volt; at 1 the modulation input tracks 1V per octave.
Modulation depth for one of the four modulation inputs into the knob it belongs to; the figure is the shift a plus or minus 10V signal produces.
Shifts the pitch in whole octaves, three either way.
Widens the unison detune range from 100 cents to 1200 cents.

inputs.text: Sets the pitch at 1V per octave; the PITCH knob is added to it.
A trigger resets the oscillator the way a new note does; with a one-shot wavetable loaded it starts the one shot again.
Carries a modulation signal; arm it with its button, then turn a knob to set how far this signal moves that knob.

outputs.text: The left channel of the oscillator; with a single unison voice the same signal appears on both channels.
The right channel of the oscillator.

notes: The wavetable in use is named along the bottom of the display. The arrow at each end of that strip moves one wavetable along the list, and clicking the name between them opens the whole list.
A modulation input does nothing until you press the button above it to arm it and then drag a knob; the drag sets how far that input moves that knob, and a ring on the knob shows the amount.
menu: Wavetables — a submenu listing the factory wavetable categories, and carrying the items that load your own.
Load Wavetable File — in the Wavetables submenu, opens a file dialog for a .wav or .wt wavetable.
Load WaveEdit Wavetable — in the Wavetables submenu, loads a .wav file read as a WaveEdit table of 256 sample frames.
Load Untagged Wav as — in the Wavetables submenu, loads a plain .wav file cut into frames of the length you pick, from 64 to 4096 samples.
Download Extra Wavetable Content — in the Wavetables submenu, fetches the extra Surge wavetable set over the network.
Reveal Rack User Wavetables Directory — in the Wavetables submenu, opens the folder your own wavetables are read from.
Rescan Wavetables — in the Wavetables submenu, reads the wavetable folders again so files added since startup appear.
Retrigger With Phase=0 — restarts every unison voice from the same phase when the oscillator is retriggered.
Extend Unison Detune — widens the unison detune range to 1200 cents.
Absolute Unison Detune — measures the unison spread in hertz rather than in cents.
Character — a submenu setting a fixed filter on the output: Warm, Neutral or Bright.
Oscillator Drift — a slider in the menu setting how much slow random pitch wander is added, as a percentage.
Output Level — a slider in the menu attenuating the oscillator's output, as a percentage.
Halfband Filter — a submenu choosing the downsampling filter used on the oversampled oscillator, from M = 6, steep to M = 1, shallow.
Apply DC Blocker — switches on the high pass that removes any DC offset from the output.
Curve Poly Channel — a submenu choosing which polyphonic channel the display draws, Ch 1 to Ch 16.
Use Global Style — ties this module's appearance to the setting shared by every Surge XT module, rather than to this module alone.
Skin — sets the panel colouring: Dark, Medium or Light.
Colors — a submenu setting the colour of the Display Area, Knob and Slider Values, Modulations and Power Buttons, and carrying Show Knob Shadows.
Value Displays — a submenu carrying Knob Value Rings, Knob Modulation Animations and Display Modulation Animations.
